facts.claim: Croajingolong is a coastal national park in East Gippsland; its name comes from the Krauatungalung words galung ('belonging to') and kraua ('east').
The park is linear, about 80 km by 20 km, bordered by the Tasman Sea to the south and the Bemm River to the west, with Mallacoota at its eastern end.
Landscapes include rocky outcrops, long sandy beaches, coastal dunes and freshwater rivers, popular for hiking, swimming, snorkelling and sea kayaking.
UNESCO nominated it a World Biosphere Reserve in 1977; it holds almost 1,000 native plant species and 315 animal species.
The Wilderness Coast Walk runs along the park's coast (about 100 km per Wikipedia); the popular section is 45 km from Thurra River to Shipwreck Creek.
Point Hicks is believed to be Captain Cook's first Australian landfall, with Southern Ocean views; Point Hicks Lighthouse has keepers' cottages to stay in.

experiences: Walk a wild coast of empty beaches

tips.title: Bring your own food
tips.detail: Outside Mallacoota there is nowhere to eat or buy supplies in the park, so stock up in town before heading in.

tips.title: Unsealed roads need 4WD
tips.detail: Mallacoota is the only town and the park has no other paved roads. Reaching places like Point Hicks needs a good 4WD.

tips.title: Permit for Wilderness Coast
tips.detail: Get a Parks Victoria permit before attempting the multi-day Wilderness Coast Walk. Entry to the park itself has no fee.

best_months.rationale: Derived: warm months suit beach, paddling and camping on an exposed coast; no source states best months (UNVERIFIED).

facts.claim: Ararat is about 200 km north-west of Melbourne on the Western Highway and is known as the Gateway to the Grampians.
Gold found in 1857 turned it into a boomtown; it is the only city in Australia founded by Chinese people, a history told at the Gum San Chinese Heritage Centre.
Visitors can tour J Ward, the former home of the criminally insane, and the Aradale asylum.
Seppelt at Great Western, a short drive away, has 3 km of 1800s tunnels, the largest underground cellar in the Southern Hemisphere.
Several wineries lie within 30 minutes' drive, including Cathcart Ridge, Langi Ghiran and Best's.
Climate: warm summers frequently interrupted by cold fronts, and cool, usually rainy winters.

experiences: Tour the old asylum and J Ward

tips.title: Train from Melbourne
tips.detail: V/Line runs trains from Southern Cross several times daily, and The Overland to Adelaide stops twice a week.

tips.title: Book cellar tours
tips.detail: Seppelt's tunnel tours run at set times (11am, 1pm, 3pm per the guide) for a fee, so check times before driving out.

best_months.rationale: Derived from the climate (warm summers with cold fronts, cool rainy winters): autumn and spring suit touring wineries and heritage sites (UNVERIFIED as a guide recommendation).

facts.claim: Warrnambool is the largest town in south-west Victoria, about 260 km west of Melbourne, with a population of 35,000, and is sometimes treated as the end of the Great Ocean Road.
Southern right whales can be seen from the Logans Beach platform between June and September, often without binoculars.
Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum has a replica maritime village and a night show telling the story of the Loch Ard wreck.
Tower Hill, 14 km west, is an extinct volcano that erupted at least 34,000 years ago and is now a wildlife reserve.
Moyjil (Point Ritchie) is a headland at the Hopkins River mouth and a significant Aboriginal site used for thousands of years.
A 37 km rail trail links Warrnambool and Port Fairy via Koroit.

experiences: Watch southern right whales from shore
Walk the rim of an extinct volcano
Cycle the rail trail to Port Fairy

tips.title: Whale season June-September
tips.detail: Southern right whales visit Logans Beach from June to September. Check the visitor centre for confirmed sightings.

tips.title: Allow time to drive
tips.detail: Melbourne is about 3.5 hours by the Princes Highway and longer along the Great Ocean Road, so plan an overnight.

best_months.rationale: Whale watching season at Logans Beach is June to September.

destinations.seasonal_tags: whale watching Jun-Sep (yearly pattern, WV Warrnambool)

facts.claim: The Mornington Peninsula lies south of Melbourne on the eastern side of Port Phillip Bay, about 40 km long and 15-20 km wide before tapering to Point Nepean.
Arthurs Seat reaches 305 m and has a summit road with wide views.
Peninsula Hot Springs has mineral-rich thermal pools up to 50C at Fingal.
The bay side has sheltered sandy beaches for families, while the ocean side is popular with surfers.
Point Nepean has an old fort and quarantine station, and is where Prime Minister Harold Holt vanished while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967.
The Two Bays Walking Track is 26 km from Dromana to Cape Schanck; the Bushrangers Bay walk offers a good chance of seeing kangaroos.
Wineries, mazes and water sports are among the main attractions.

experiences: Walk coastal cliffs and bay beaches

tips.title: Drive or ferry in
tips.detail: Public transport is limited beyond the main towns, so a car helps. The Sorrento-Queenscliff car ferry runs hourly, 7am-6pm.

tips.title: Pack a jacket in winter
tips.detail: Summer is busiest, but cold-season storms on the Bass Strait beaches are dramatic. Bring a jacket.

tips.title: Hot springs book out
tips.detail: Peninsula Hot Springs charges peak-time prices, and under-5s were not admitted per the guide, so check before taking children.

best_months.rationale: The peninsula is at its best and busiest in summer.
